subject: Post-demo: deployment-mode decision matrix & migration scope
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Wu <caroline.wu@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Simon Patel <simon@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2025-03-15T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: deployment-mode decision matrix & migration scope

Hi Caroline — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from our call plus proposed next steps so we can align on hosting and migration approach.

Recap (customer constraints)
- PHI scope: pilot will include limited EHR extracts and PII-containing clinical notes.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 250ms per token for internal triage flows; batch scoring can be higher.
- Throughput: steady-state target ~15–25 QPS, with occasional bursts to 50 QPS.
- Regulatory: require audit logs, customer-managed KMS, and SOC2 evidence; potential BAA.
- Existing deployment: currently calling another LLM API (OpenAI) for generation; some teams run a legacy on-prem GPU cluster for research.

Redwood-hosting options (short):
- Hosted API (fastest): low-friction onboarding, immediate access to model catalog. Good for early POC but recommend only if PHI is excluded or a BAA is in place and Atlas is comfortable with Redwood-managed keys.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools (Redwood-managed infra) with single-tenant capacity. Predictable throughput and stronger isolation; supports customer-configurable auth, audit trails, and SLA uplift. Good middle ground for PHI if you need throughput guarantees but not full VPC control.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-controlled VPC and optional on-prem package. Supports customer-managed KMS/HSM, private network peering, and air-gapped deployments. Best fit for regulated PHI workloads.

Migration notes (from other APIs / self-hosted)
- From other public LLM APIs: usually straightforward at the request/response level, but we recommend a compatibility adapter for prompt templates, tokenization differences, and response-parsing checks. Expect a warm-up period to populate caches (KV/prefix cache) and to rebuild rate-limiting/batching profiles.
- From self-hosted GPU clusters: model artifact compatibility and quantization may require re-compile or re-quantization. We'll need model version artifacts and estimates of peak sequence lengths. Runtime kernels differ; we usually run a short compatibility pass to validate perf parity.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan)
1) You: confirm preferred hosting lane (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and share procurement timeline.
2) You: return the attached security questionnaire (Atlas_Security_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx) — we can pre-fill some fields.
3) Redwood: schedule a technical deep-dive (Monica + Aditya) to capture traffic patterns, model list, and retention/SLOs. (~60–90 min)
4) Redwood: deliver a deployment matrix + ballpark cost and timeline (2–3 business days after deep-dive).
5) Pilot: 4–8 week pilot depending on hosting choice (Dedicated shorter; Private longer).

Attachments: Atlas_Security_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx (attached), atlas_infra_diagram.pdf (attached).

Would Monday or Tuesday next week work for the technical deep-dive? I’ve cc’d Simon so procurement visibility is present.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

Hi Sean — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying questions before we lock a deep-dive:

1) PHI & compliance: which of the three lanes support PHI out of the box? Do you provide a BAA for Hosted? Is HSM/KMS customer-managed available for Dedicated or Hosted?
2) Auditability: can Dedicated/Private deliver the level of audit logs we need (per-request metadata, model version, user id, token counts) and how long are logs retained by default?
3) Migration effort: for our team that’s currently on the OpenAI endpoints, what is the expected work to reach parity (templates, prompt tuning, E2E testing)? Similarly, for the research cluster — are there blockers to bringing models over?
4) Costs: ballpark unit economics for token cost across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (we understand final will vary). Any guidance on egress/networking fees?

Attached: Atlas_procurement_timeline_v1.docx (for visibility).

Simon and I prefer a deep-dive on Tuesday afternoon if that’s available. Also please indicate what info you need from us to scope the pilot.

Cheers,

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Wu <caroline.wu@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Simon Patel <simon@atlashealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-03-16T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment-mode decision matrix & migration scope

Caroline — great questions. Short answers up front, then a recommended approach.

PHI & compliance
- Hosted: we offer BAAs and can support PHI processing but only with specific contractual controls and region restrictions; Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default but can be configured to use customer-managed keys for certain enterprise plans (needs contract review).
- Dedicated: supports customer-configurable key management options, audit logging, and SLA uplifts. Many customers with sensitive data choose Dedicated as a compromise between speed and control.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): supports full customer-managed KMS/HSM and private peering; recommended if Atlas requires strict network isolation or air-gapped environments.

Audit logs & retention
- We can provide per-request audit trails (timestamp, caller id, model version, token counts, latency). Default retention: 90 days in Hosted; configurable longer retention options for Dedicated and Private. We can add log export to your SIEM via S3 or streaming.

Migration effort
- From OpenAI: typical path = compatibility adapter layer + test harness. Work includes: tokenization parity checks, prompt template alignment, and golden-response tests. Estimated effort: 2–4 engineer-weeks for a straightforward integration + 1–2 weeks of testing and validation. Cache warming can add 1–2 weeks for steady-state performance.
- From self-hosted GPU cluster: depends on model artifact portability. If you can provide model weights and tokenizer configs, we can evaluate runtime compatibility. Common blockers: unsupported quantization formats and custom kernels. We typically run a model onboarding pass (2–3 weeks) to confirm perf/accuracy and then a short re-quantization step if needed.

Costs & egress
- Hosted: per-token base price (lowest friction).
- Dedicated: committed monthly capacity, lower per-token unit cost at scale; pricing depends on reserved GPU tier.
- Private: higher fixed platform/licensing + infra costs; per-token cost depends on local infra economics.
- Egress: if you peer via Private VPC, egress is handled via your cloud account (no additional Redwood egress on Private). For Hosted/Dedicated, cloud egress charges may apply depending on region — we can estimate after we know traffic volumes.

Recommended approach (based on constraints)
1) Short-term POC (Dedicated): reserve a small Dedicated pool to validate latency, throughput, and SLOs with Atlas data (non-PHI subset if you prefer). Minimal procurement friction vs Private and quicker ramp (4–6 weeks).
2) Parallel security evaluation: we’ll complete the security questionnaire, and you can surface any non-negotiables that would push us to Private.
3) Migration plan: run an adapter-based integration for OpenAI parity + golden-tests. For the self-hosted models, provide artifacts and we’ll run an onboarding pass.

Proposed times: Monica/Aditya are available Tue 2025-03-18 at 2pm PT for a technical deep-dive and to collect required artifacts. Items we need from Atlas for scoping:
- sample request volumes (QPS patterns) + p95 latency targets
- list of models (name, approximate size) you want in pilot
- expected token/month estimate and retention policy
- any network constraints (must be VPC-only, firewall rules)

If that timing works I’ll send a calendar invite and a short intake form to speed the deep-dive.

Attachments referenced: I’ll return the security questionnaire with pre-filled answers after the deep-dive.

Thanks — Sean

Thanks Sean — jumping in to operationalize the deep-dive. To make the POC estimate useful, please ask Atlas to provide the following before the call:
- 2 weeks of representative traffic logs (anonymized) or a shaped traffic profile (requests/sec, avg tokens/request, p95 sequence length)
- Target SLOs (latency p50/p95, error budget) and any per-request trace attributes required in audit logs
- List of models and whether they are vendor-managed (OpenAI, Anthropic) or customer-provided artifacts (weights + tokenizer)
- Data retention policy and expected retention window for audit logs/requests
- Expected go/no-go criteria for pilot (latency targets, quality thresholds, cost thresholds)

We can draft a deployment matrix that compares Hosted / Dedicated / Private across controls (KMS/HSM, network isolation, audit retention, SLA, rollout time, cost band). If Monday/Tuesday next week is requested previously, Monica here prefers Tue 2025-03-18 2pm PT. I’ll attach a short intake form in the calendar invite.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
